strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.2.10	mercy makes a people	The commentary says a group receives favor while another strays; Peter says those once not a people have become God's people and those without mercy have received mercy.
strong	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:1Pet.3.12	the Lord's face against evil	The commentary says the face carries the sign of wrath or favor; Peter says the Lord's eyes are on the righteous and his face is against those who do evil, applying the contrast to Christian conduct.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.15.4	the shepherd seeks the lost	The commentary names those who stray and asks for guidance; Jesus depicts a shepherd going after one lost sheep until he finds it, turning the straying image into a search for restoration.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.15.7	joy when the lost repents	The commentary says some receive forgiveness rather than wrath; Jesus says heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents, interpreting recovery of the lost as joy rather than rejection.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.4.5	praise given when the Lord comes	The commentary glosses hamd as praise and approval and names the day of recompense; Paul says the Lord's coming reveals hidden motives and each person then receives praise from God.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.29	praise from God, not people	The commentary describes hamd as approval; Paul says the true inward Jew receives praise from God rather than from human beings.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.12.43	human approval preferred to God's	The commentary asks whose judgment one approves and sets God's favor against anger; John says some loved human glory more than God's glory, explaining their refusal to confess Jesus.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.1.10	pleasing people or God	The commentary connects praise with approval and divine pleasure; Paul asks whether he seeks human approval or God's and says pleasing people would make him no servant of Christ.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.5.9	aim to please the Lord	The commentary opens the scene with divine pleasure and closes it with judgment; Paul says his aim is to please the Lord before describing the judgment seat in the next verse.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Cor.5.10	each appears before the judgment seat	The commentary names the day of recompense; Paul says all must appear before Christ's judgment seat and receive according to what they did.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Phil.2.13	God works for his good pleasure	The commentary says the favored gift is actively bestowed; Paul says God works within the community both to will and to work for his good pleasure.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.5.28	the dead hear and come out	The commentary names the day of recompense for groups with different outcomes; Jesus speaks of the hour when all in the tombs hear his voice and come out.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.5.29	resurrection to life or judgment	The commentary divides the judged into opposite destinations; Jesus says those who did good rise to life and those who did evil rise to judgment.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.4	the day does not overtake children of light	The commentary pairs the judgment day with faces that reveal each group's outcome; Paul says believers are not in darkness for the day to overtake them like a thief.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.5	children of day and light	The commentary divides the guided from the straying; Paul calls the community children of light and children of day, not of night or darkness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.7	relief for the afflicted at revelation	The commentary sets wrath against the reward of the guided; Paul says the afflicted will receive relief when Jesus is revealed from heaven.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.8	punishment at the Lord's revelation	The commentary names wrath coming upon a group; Paul describes punishment for those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel when the Lord is revealed.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.10	glory among the saints	The commentary names prophets, martyrs, and the righteous as companions; Paul says Christ comes to be glorified among his saints and marveled at by those who believed.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.23	assembly of the righteous in heaven	The commentary lists prophets, truth-affirmers, martyrs, and righteous companions; Hebrews describes the assembly of the firstborn and the spirits of righteous people made complete.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.13	blessed dead whose deeds follow them	The commentary names martyrs among those receiving favor; Revelation calls the dead who die in the Lord blessed, says they rest from toil, and says their deeds follow them.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.20.4	martyrs share judgment and reign	The commentary includes martyrs among the favored companions; Revelation pictures those slain for their testimony seated on thrones, given judgment, and reigning with Christ.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.20.12	books opened for the dead	The commentary names the day of recompense; Revelation depicts the dead standing before the throne while books are opened and they are judged by their deeds.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.20.15	book of life and the opposite end	The commentary divides groups by their final outcome; Revelation says those not found in the book of life are thrown into the lake of fire.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.3	no more curse	The commentary contrasts wrath with favor and the guided with the lost; Revelation's final city has no more curse, and God's servants worship there.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.22.4	see God's face	The commentary says faces display the outcome of judgment; Revelation describes the servants seeing God's face and bearing his name on their foreheads.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Phil.2.15	shining lights among a crooked generation	The commentary contrasts the favored path with those who stray and says faces may shine; Paul calls believers blameless children of God who shine like lights in a crooked generation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.1.12	share the inheritance of the saints in light	The commentary names prophets and righteous among the favored; Paul gives thanks that believers are qualified to share the inheritance of the saints in light.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.1.13	transferred from darkness into the Son's kingdom	The commentary contrasts the guided with those who stray; Paul says God rescued people from darkness and transferred them into the kingdom of his beloved Son, where there is redemption and forgiveness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.1.6	walking in darkness denies fellowship	The commentary distinguishes a guided way from straying; John says claiming fellowship while walking in darkness is falsehood.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.1.7	walking in light brings cleansing	The commentary connects the favored way with a visible sign of well-being; John says walking in the light brings fellowship and cleansing from sin.

medium	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 5:11	anger measured by capacity to reconcile	The commentary sets anger against pleasure and describes its bodily face; Avot distinguishes temperaments by how readily a person becomes angry and how readily they are appeased.
medium	tevrat	motif	b. Shabbat 105b	anger enacted through destructive acts	The commentary describes anger as an inward heat with outward bodily signs; the Talmud warns against tearing clothes, breaking vessels, or scattering money in anger, treating those acts as a dangerous loss of moral control.
medium	tevrat	motif	b. Yoma 85b	neighbor's grievance before atonement	The commentary juxtaposes wrath, pardon, and the way one should follow; this teaching says atonement for wrongs against another person requires first appeasing the injured neighbor.

medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.147.11	divine pleasure toward those who hope in love	The source commentary frames wrath opposite divine pleasure; the psalm says the Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him and hope in his steadfast love, a positive community receiving favor.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.149.4	favor toward the humble	The source commentary contrasts divine wrath with divine pleasure; the psalm says the Lord takes pleasure in his people and adorns the humble with salvation.
medium	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Matt.6.16	a face can be deliberately disfigured	The commentary reads faces as signs of inward outcomes; Jesus warns that hypocrites disfigure their faces to display fasting, showing that a visible religious face can be staged for human notice.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.6.17	wash your face in secret	The commentary gives the face a role in visible favor or wrath; Jesus tells the fasting person to wash and anoint the face so devotion is not performed for human observers.
